text: Now for the science segment, and we're starting with something that's literally happening above our heads tonight. That blue moon Jamie mentioned earlier isn't just pretty to look at - it's peak illumination at 4:45 AM EDT gives us the perfect excuse to talk about some seriously clever space science. Researchers have also just figured out how pigeons navigate using iron-filled immune cells in their liver that act like tiny magnetic sensors.

speaker: alice
text: Birds with built-in GPS, essentially! But the real breakthrough today is this quantum detector that's solving what scientists call the terahertz gap. This specially designed metasurface funnels incoming energy into tiny active regions, making terahertz radiation much easier to detect. It's one of those discoveries that sounds super technical but could revolutionize everything from medical imaging to communications.

speaker: charlie
text: And here's one for the health buffs - a new study shows fish oil might help reduce insulin resistance even in people who aren't obese. In diabetic rats, omega-3 supplementation improved blood sugar, cholesterol, and inflammation by shifting immune cells into a more helpful mode. Sometimes the old remedies really are the best ones, just with better science behind them now.
